answer: Persistent Behavioural Anchor Rule: each identity carries a rolling history of task outcomes and interaction partners. To re-register, an agent must present a valid, verifiable trajectory whose interaction graph overlaps its prior epochs, so fresh identities cannot wander into the system unanchored. Anchors propagate like a nebula of linked records, and any identity whose chain lacks continuity is rejected at the gateway. The beacon for admission is thus cross-epoch linkage, not a one-time credential.
